I've written the network, and `build.py`, `weights.npz` and `explanation.md` are in the folder. It has never played the real game; I only tested it on frames I drew myself and in a rough simulator I wrote, so its real score is unknown. My prediction is an average of **about 4** (kills minus 1 for the death), with low confidence and a likely range of 1 to 8. `build.py` runs in under a second and the weights pass the harness's own shape check.

**What it does:** it spins left forever and never turns right, so it can't get stuck swinging back and forth. It fires only when the centre of the screen, right at eye level, is a different colour from most of 8 narrow strips of wall spread across the screen. It never fires while the pistol's muzzle flash is visible.

- **The aim test:** both centre columns have to differ from the wall, which means the monster covers the line the bullet travels along, so it doesn't fire at monsters it would miss.
- **Comparing against many wall strips:** I don't know the wall's colour, so the network takes a vote. Another monster standing in one or two of the strips doesn't change the decision.
- **Ignoring corpses:** the row it relies on most is just above eye level. Standing monsters always reach it and bodies on the floor never do, so it won't keep shooting a corpse until the ammo runs out.
- **The flash rule:** this is meant to stop the pistol automatically firing a second shot at a monster that is already dying.
- **Close monsters:** a separate check, higher up the screen, catches a monster that is right next to the player.

**What I checked:** on drawn frames it fires at a centred monster from far away (480 units) right down to touching distance. It holds fire on empty wall, on monsters 6° or more off centre, on corpses at any distance, and while the flash is showing. In the simulator it gets about 0.6 to 0.7 kills per bullet.

**Main risks:**
- **The status bar:** the design assumes the scenario draws the bar at the bottom of the screen,
